message.content: I'm getting a KeyError when my Flask app tries to read from the session dict

content.text: A KeyError on Flask session usually means the key doesn't exist yet. Use session.get('key') instead of session['key'] to return None when missing. Can you share the relevant code?

message.content: Here's the route: @app.route('/dashboard') def dashboard(): user_id = session['user_id'] return render_template('dashboard.html', uid=user_id)

The issue is that session['user_id'] raises KeyError when the user hasn't logged in. Add a login_required check or use session.get('user_id'). Also make sure you have a SECRET_KEY set in your Flask config.
I have SECRET_KEY set. The error only happens after I restart the server. Why would that cause it?

content.text: If you restart with a different SECRET_KEY, Flask cannot decrypt the old session cookie and clears it — so session['user_id'] is gone. Make sure your SECRET_KEY is stable across restarts (load from environment variable, not a random value generated at startup).

message.content: Oh! I have SECRET_KEY = os.urandom(24) in my config. That generates a new key every restart, right?

content.text: Exactly — os.urandom(24) is a new random key every time the module loads. Change it to load from an environment variable: SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get('FLASK_SECRET_KEY', 'dev-only-fallback'). For production, set a real stable key.

message.content: That fixed it! Now the sessions persist across restarts. One more thing — how do I set session expiry?

content.text: Set PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME in your config (a timedelta), then call session.permanent = True when you set up the session. Example: app.config['PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME'] = timedelta(hours=24)

message.content: Perfect. Thanks for walking me through all of this — I understand Flask sessions much better now.
Happy to help! The key points: stable SECRET_KEY from env, use session.get() defensively, and set PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME for expiry.
